subject: maths
title: Area and Perimeter
seo_title: Year 4 Area and Perimeter Worksheets: Rectilinear Shapes and Counting Squares
standard_text: Measure and calculate the perimeter of a rectilinear figure (including squares) in centimetres and metres; find the area of rectilinear shapes by counting squares.
meta_desc: Free Year 4 area and perimeter worksheets for the National Curriculum: perimeter of rectangles, squares and rectilinear shapes in cm and m, missing sides, area by counting squares and word problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Perimeter is the distance round the edge. Area is the number of squares inside.
key_sub: Add every side to find the perimeter, in cm or m. Count the squares to find the area, in squares or cm². For an L-shape, find the missing sides first.
body_html:
Perimeter and area

Perimeter is the distance all the way round a shape. It is a length, so it is in cm or m.

Area is the space inside a shape. In Year 4 we find it by counting squares. If each square is 1 cm², the area is in cm².

Perimeter of a rectangle

Add all 4 sides. A rectangle has 2 long sides and 2 short sides.

Perimeter on a grid

Count the sides of the squares round the edge, not the squares. A corner square has 2 sides on the edge.

Rectilinear shapes: find the missing sides

A rectilinear shape has only straight sides and right angles, like an L. Opposite parts add up: the short sides on one side match the long side opposite.

Example

A rectangle is 12 m long and 5 m wide. What is its perimeter?

12 + 5 + 12 + 5 = 34. Or 12 + 5 = 17, then double it: 17 + 17 = 34.

Answer: 34 m

Area by counting squares

Count the squares inside, row by row. Two half squares make one whole square.

Shortcut for a rectangle: 3 rows of 5 squares is 3 × 5 = 15 squares. You will learn this as a formula in Year 5.

Same area, different perimeter

Rectangles 6 cm by 2 cm and 4 cm by 3 cm both have an area of 12 cm². Their perimeters are 16 cm and 14 cm. A long, thin shape has a longer perimeter.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding only two sides (9 + 4 = 13 cm)Add all 4 sides: 9 + 4 + 9 + 4 = 26 cm
Counting squares to find the perimeterCount the sides of the squares round the edge
Counting a corner square only onceA corner square has 2 sides on the edge
Missing a side in an L-shapeFind the missing side first, then add all 6 sides
Mixing up area and perimeterArea = squares inside. Perimeter = distance round
Writing cm for an areaArea is in squares or cm². Perimeter is in cm

faq.q: What do Year 4 children learn about area and perimeter?
faq.a: They measure and calculate the perimeter of rectilinear shapes, including squares, in centimetres and metres, and find the area of rectilinear shapes by counting squares.
A shape with only straight sides that meet at right angles, such as a rectangle or an L-shape. You can find its perimeter by adding all the sides.

faq.q: How do you find a missing side on an L-shape?
faq.a: Use the side opposite it. The short sides on one side add up to the long side opposite, so subtract the side you know from the long side.

faq.q: Do Year 4 pupils use length × width for area?
faq.a: In Year 4 they count squares. Spotting that 3 rows of 5 squares is 3 × 5 = 15 is a good shortcut; the area formula for rectangles is taught in Year 5.

items.q: Maya’s family puts a fence round their rectangular garden. The garden is 14 m long and 9 m wide. How much fence do they need?
items.e: The fence goes along all 4 sides: 14 + 9 + 14 + 9 = 46 m.

items.q: A rectangular flower bed has a perimeter of 30 m. One side is 9 m long. How long is the side next to it?
items.e: The two 9 m sides make 18 m. 30 − 18 = 12 m for the other two sides, so each is 12 ÷ 2 = 6 m. Check: 9 + 6 + 9 + 6 = 30 m.

items.q: Freya has 1 m of ribbon. She puts ribbon round the edge of a card that is 20 cm by 12 cm. How much ribbon is left?
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm. Perimeter of the card: 20 + 12 + 20 + 12 = 64 cm. Left: 100 − 64 = 36 cm.

items.q: A chessboard has 8 rows of 8 squares. How many squares are there on the board?
items.e: 8 rows of 8 squares: 8 × 8 = 64 squares. (32 is the number of square sides round the edge.)

items.q: Noah has 16 m of fence to make a rectangular pen for his rabbits. Which pen gives the rabbits the most space?
items.e: All four pens use 16 m of fence. Areas: 7 × 1 = 7 m², 6 × 2 = 12 m², 5 × 3 = 15 m², 4 × 4 = 16 m². The square has the most space.

items.q: Charlie glues ribbon round the edge of a photo frame. The frame is 20 cm long and 15 cm wide. How much ribbon does he need?
items.e: Ribbon goes round the edge, so find the perimeter: 20 + 15 + 20 + 15 = 70 cm.

items.q: In PE, Mohammed runs round a rectangular field 2 times. The field is 25 m long and 15 m wide. How far does he run?
items.e: Once round: 25 + 15 + 25 + 15 = 80 m. Two times round: 2 × 80 = 160 m.

items.q: Poppy wants to put coloured tape round the edge of a picture. What should she work out?
items.e: Tape goes round the edge, so find the perimeter. Perimeter is a length, so it is in cm.

items.q: A rectangular vegetable patch is 12 m long and 8 m wide. A fence goes all the way round, except for a gate that is 2 m wide. How much fence is needed?
items.e: Perimeter: 12 + 8 + 12 + 8 = 40 m. There is no fence across the gate: 40 − 2 = 38 m.

items.q: A display board in the classroom is 120 cm long and 90 cm wide. The teacher puts a paper border round the edge. How long is the border?
items.e: Border round the edge = perimeter: 120 + 90 + 120 + 90 = 420 cm.

items.q: The school playground is a rectangle 30 m long and 20 m wide. How far is it once round the edge?
items.e: Once round is the perimeter: 30 + 20 + 30 + 20 = 100 m.

items.q: A football pitch is 100 m long and 60 m wide. The team jogs once round the edge. How far is that?
A patio is made of square paving slabs. Each slab is 1 m by 1 m. There are 5 rows of 4 slabs. What is the area of the patio?
items.e: Count the slabs: 5 rows of 4 is 5 × 4 = 20 slabs, so the area is 20 m².

items.q: A vegetable patch is split into 1 m squares: 6 rows of 4 squares. Carrots grow in 5 squares and potatoes in the rest. What area is potatoes?
items.e: Whole patch: 6 × 4 = 24 m². Take away the carrots: 24 − 5 = 19 m².

items.q: A square sandpit has a perimeter of 20 m. How long is each side?
items.e: A square has 4 equal sides: 20 ÷ 4 = 5 m. Check: 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 = 20 m.

items.q: Isla puts ribbon round a square photo frame. Each side is 18 cm. How much ribbon does she need?
items.e: A square has 4 equal sides: 4 × 18 = 72 cm.

items.q: Amelia wants to cover the front of a book with paper. What should she work out?
items.e: Covering the inside of a shape is area. Area is counted in squares, so it is in cm².

items.q: A square garden has sides of 6 m. Fence panels are 2 m long. How many panels go all the way round?
items.e: Perimeter: 4 × 6 = 24 m. Each panel is 2 m: 24 ÷ 2 = 12 panels.

items.q: A classroom floor is covered with square carpet tiles. Each tile is 1 m long and 1 m wide. There are 7 rows of 9 tiles. What is the area of the floor?
items.e: Each tile is 1 m², so count the tiles: 7 rows of 9 is 7 × 9 = 63 m².

items.q: This is the plan of an L-shaped garden. Two sides are not labelled. How much fence goes all the way round?
items.e: Missing sides: 12 − 7 = 5 m and 9 − 5 = 4 m. Add all 6 sides: 5 + 5 + 7 + 4 + 12 + 9 = 42 m.
